facts_transferred.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
facts_transferred.fact: For an 80 psf service gravity load, each seat supporting a paired floor truss carried approximately 16 kip. NIST Table 4-2 gives 20 C interior-seat vertical capacities from 194 to 395 kip.

facts_transferred.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
facts_transferred.fact: NIST Table 4-3 gives 20 C exterior-seat vertical capacities from 94 to 207 kip for the eight Floor 96 details studied.

facts_transferred.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
facts_transferred.fact: Immediately after impact, the modeled core-load increase was 400 kip at both Floor 98 and Floor 105, so the differential change attributable to the core-to-wall path between those levels was zero. At 80 min, the modeled core load decreased by 6,748 kip at Floor 98 and 6,783 kip at Floor 105.

facts_transferred.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
facts_transferred.fact: In the Case B hat-truss checks, outrigger E reached DCR 0.97 at 80 min; the listed exterior columns supporting the outriggers remained below DCR 0.67 at 80 min.
facts_transferred.confidence: high; Table 4-27 and Table 4-28 visually checked

facts_transferred.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
facts_transferred.fact: All 22 primary-path hat-truss connections listed by NIST were classified safe at 80 min; published demands and yield/ultimate capacities are retained in the V8G component dataset.

facts_transferred.label: FAIT_ET_RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
facts_transferred.fact: NIST reports 38 of 59 north-wall columns, three of 59 south-wall columns, and nine of 47 core columns severed or heavily damaged. It also reports severe north office-floor damage between perimeter Columns 112 and 145 on Floors 94-98. In the global model, the core carried about one percent more load immediately after impact.
facts_transferred.confidence: high for the reported damage/model result; this does not provide a surviving truss-seat map

facts_transferred.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
facts_transferred.fact: Each tower face had 59 perimeter columns at 40 in spacing. The built-up box section was approximately 14 in square, but plate thickness varied by location.

facts_transferred.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL_LIMITE
facts_transferred.fact: Recovered WTC 1 perimeter Column 142 over Floors 97-100 was specified Fy = 60 ksi. This specimen does not establish all perimeter sections or plate thicknesses around Floors 94-99.
facts_transferred.confidence: high for the specimen; low for generalization

model_assumptions.inherited_core_network: V8I nearest-four proxy, 47 reconstructed core-column nodes and the cold_upper_envelope cracked-slab case
model_assumptions.cold_demand: NIST Case B Floor 98 after-impact core load, 34,429 kip
model_assumptions.cut_set_definition: At the first cold failure, remove every core proxy edge whose beam and membrane branches have both fractured; identify any loaded connected component containing no surviving column support
model_assumptions.paired_truss_count_full_face: tower width divided by 6.67 ft paired-truss tributary width, rounded to 31
model_assumptions.north_surviving_pair_proxy: 31 multiplied by 21/59 surviving north-wall columns, rounded to 11; this is a sensitivity proxy, not a seat-by-seat impact map
model_assumptions.seat_bridge_test: The isolated cut load is divided by each published 20 C exterior-seat capacity. This is a capacity-only screening test and does not assert compatible stiffness, ductility, geometry, or survival of the floor path.
model_assumptions.hat_truss_cold_rule: No additional cold core unloading is credited because NIST Table 4-22 reports the same +400 kip core-load change at Floors 98 and 105. The hat truss can redistribute wall loads while its net differential core transfer is zero.

gate_definition.required_condition: The post-impact 20 C model must have a mechanically specified, surviving force-displacement path for every loaded component before thermal studies or Blender coupling.
gate_definition.pass_policy: Capacity arithmetic alone cannot pass the gate. The path topology, stiffness, deformation capacity, connection assignment, and impact survival must all be specified from drawings or a declared validated substitute.

office_floor_to_perimeter_capacity_scree.interpretation: The full-face arithmetic envelope straddles the cut demand, while the 11-pair north-damage proxy does not pass for any published exterior seat detail. Neither result proves a physical bridge because the actual seat map, floor-truss stiffness, load compatibility and impact survival of the path are not established.

hat_truss_path.interpretation: The hat truss was mechanically active after impact and redistributed wall loads, but the official tables do not show net differential core unloading at the cold post-impact state. Crediting the later 6,748 kip transfer to the cold gate would double count a thermal-time response.

gate_result.reason: V8J quantifies a loaded disconnected component and finds that published capacity envelopes straddle its demand, but the actual surviving topology, stiffness, ductility and connection assignment are not available.
